briefs.covers: C1-C5, original freeze plus R24 widening
TESSGUARD_DB_PATH marker-file write (C6 amendment). Brief marker updated to this ticket; DEVH-35 remains cited here.

done_state: install-dev-harness.sh installs a working hooks/skills/agents set into a fresh machine's ~/.claude/ tree, substitutes every /path/to/... token with the real local path, and fails closed (nonzero exit, no partial install left in place) if any required file is missing from the source tree -- including every real persona file in agents/, not a hardcoded subset of it. AND (R24, DEVH-2): the preflight refuses to install a tree missing any one of the three security guards, and a guard installed by that installer denies a destructive command from its installed location, not merely from the build tree.

criteria.statement: install-dev-harness.sh exits nonzero and prints a 'required hook missing' message when a required hook file is absent from the source tree, rather than installing a partial hooks directory silently.

Every /path/to/... token in the installed hooks tree is replaced with the real local path (HOOKS_DST/SKILLS_DST/AGENTS_DST/TESSERA_ROOT/HOME-derived), with none of the literal tokens left in installed files.

REQUIRED_AGENTS names every real file in agents/*.md, not a hardcoded subset -- so the install script's fail-closed guarantee actually covers the whole persona roster, including personas added after this list was first written.
install-dev-harness.sh's REQUIRED_HOOKS preflight names all three guards, and removing any one of them individually causes the installer to refuse to install.
criteria.verification: Three separate trials, one per guard, not one trial deleting all three -- a preflight that special-cases a single filename would pass a combined test. For each guard: copy the repository to a temp directory, delete that one guard file, run install-dev-harness.sh with HOOKS_DST, SKILLS_DST and AGENTS_DST pointed at temp paths, and assert a non-zero exit whose stderr names the missing file. Then assert an unmodified copy installs successfully, so the criterion cannot be satisfied by an installer that refuses everything.

criteria.statement: Each of the three guards, as installed by the installer, denies the traffic it exists to block when driven from its installed location.
criteria.verification: muse's fourth verification leg, and the one that separates this from a file-existence check. Run a full install into a temp HOME. Then drive the INSTALLED copy of EACH of guard_destructive.py, guard_prodconfig.py and guard_untrusted_web.py -- the files under the temp HOOKS_DST, not the repository sources -- as subprocesses with a PreToolUse payload on stdin, and assert permissionDecision == 'deny' for each. All three are required. Token substitution rewrites files individually, so a substitution that corrupts one guard's imports leaves the others working; exercising only guard_destructive.py proves that one file survived installation and says nothing about the other two. Each guard must also be shown silent on a payload outside its own surface from the installed location, so the installed copy is not merely denying everything.

criteria.statement: install-dev-harness.sh writes a per-clone TESSGUARD_DB_PATH marker file (<ROOT>/.foreman/tessguard-db-path, containing the real, resolved TESSERA_ROOT/data/tessera.db path) as part of a normal install run, so tessguard's git hooks resolve the db without requiring a manually-exported environment variable -- DEVH-56. Does not touch the user's shell profile; matches bollard/tessera_resolver.py's own existing .foreman/tessera-prefix override-file convention rather than inventing a new mechanism.
criteria.verification: python3 -m unittest scripts.test_install_fail_closed against a new test: run the real installer into a temp ROOT/HOME, assert <temp ROOT>/.foreman/tessguard-db-path exists, is a real absolute path (no /path/to/... token survives), and names a file that actually exists on disk at TESSERA_ROOT/data/tessera.db for the temp install's own TESSERA_ROOT. Companion end-to-end proof lives in tessera/GOALS.json C10 (a real git-hooks invocation with TESSGUARD_DB_PATH genuinely unset succeeding via this marker file) -- this criterion covers the install script's own half: that the file is written correctly, not the consuming side.

failure_criteria.statement: REQUIRED_AGENTS (or any other hardcoded file-name list in this script) silently drifts out of sync with the real source directory as new files are added, so the script's own 'fail closed on missing files' guarantee stops covering the full set without anyone noticing.
failure_criteria.detection: C3: derive the expected set from agents/*.md directly in the test, not from a second hardcoded list that could drift the same way the first one did. Real instance found live 2026-08-29: nadia-osei.md and owen-reyes.md (landed 2026-08-27) were both uncovered.

failure_criteria.statement: A partial install is left on disk after a fail-closed exit (files already copied before the check that fails are not cleaned up).
failure_criteria.detection: Not currently tested. Known gap: REQUIRED_HOOKS/REQUIRED_AGENTS checks run before any copy loop starts (source-tree validation), so today's fail-closed paths never leave a partial install -- but this isn't asserted by a test, it's true by the current code's ordering, which could regress silently.

failure_criteria.statement: The three guards are appended to REQUIRED_HOOKS but the preflight loop is only reached on some paths, or a later change reorders it after the copy step. Installation of a guard-free tree still succeeds and the fail-closed claim is false while the list looks right.
failure_criteria.detection: C4 runs the real installer against a real tree with a real file removed, three times, and requires a non-zero exit each time.

failure_criteria.statement: Guards are copied in but token substitution breaks their imports, so they exist at the destination and crash when invoked. Every install-time check passes and the harness runs with three hooks that raise on every call.
failure_criteria.detection: C5 executes the installed copy from its installed location.

failure_criteria.statement: The installed-guard probe covers one guard and the criterion is read as covering installation of all three. A substitution bug specific to guard_prodconfig.py or guard_untrusted_web.py -- a token appearing in only those files, say -- ships a guard that raises on every invocation, while every test passes and the install reports success.
failure_criteria.detection: C5 requires all three installed copies to be driven from the temp HOME and to deny their own traffic, plus a silence control for each.

failure_criteria.statement: The marker file is written but still carries a literal /path/to/... token (the same class of bug F1's own git history already reproduced once for REQUIRED_AGENTS/token substitution generally), or is written to the wrong location (HOOKS_DST instead of this clone's own ROOT, where tessguard's config.py actually looks for it).
failure_criteria.detection: C6 asserts the marker file both names a real, existing file on disk and contains no /path/to/... token, at the specific path <ROOT>/.foreman/tessguard-db-path -- not merely that some file got written somewhere.

out_of_scope: The content of what gets installed (hooks/skills/agents themselves) -- this component only covers the install mechanism's own correctness.
Verifying the installed hooks actually fire correctly once registered in a real settings.json -- that's the hooks' own components' job.
A live TESSERA-ticket-existence check for anything this script installs -- matches this codebase's own standing rule against gates depending on another repo's live state.
constraints: POSIX sh, not bash-specific syntax -- set -eu at the top commits to this.
Must never copy ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (explicitly logged on every run).

results.note: Verified by reading the implementation, not only by the passing count. Each probe resolves self.home / 'hooks' / guard_*.py -- the installed artifact, not the repository source -- and asserts is_file() first so a silently missing install fails rather than skipping. The untrusted_web probe resolves its tool name from the INSTALLED template via declared_tool_name_from_installed_template rather than hardcoding it, which is the same resolve-from-the-declared-matcher property bollard C7 requires. The assertion pair is discriminating by construction: an always-silent guard fails the deny case on json.loads of empty stdout, and a deny-everything guard fails the silence case on non-empty stdout. Implemented by dev-harness-33 under DEVH-38 after this criterion was widened and recorded NOT MET.

amendments.to: C6 requires install-dev-harness.sh to write a per-clone marker file (.foreman/tessguard-db-path) carrying the real, resolved db path -- the install-side half of the DEVH-56 fix. amendments.reason: Marcus Webb's fresh ship-readiness re-verification (dev-harness-7f) found TESSGUARD_DB_PATH unset anywhere persistent -- not in any shell profile, not exported by this script -- so a genuinely fresh shell fails every tessguard git-hook invocation unconditionally, ticket-citing or not, regardless of DEVH-54's own real-commit verification (which had the var manually exported in that testing session). Chosen fix shape: a per-clone marker file this script writes, read as a fallback by config.py, matching bollard/tessera_resolver.py's own .foreman/tessera-prefix override-file convention -- not an edit to the operator's shell profile, which was the other option DEVH-56 itself named but did not decide between.
